title: Scheduler reconciliation registry entry
description: One row of the control-plane registry that reconciles the two scheduling substrates. It is the single declared inventory of every scheduled job on the host, including the ones deliberately switched off.

owner_layer.description: Which substrate actually runs it. A runtime job cannot supervise the runtime; a host service can, because it survives a gateway restart.

lifecycle_state.description: Classification is explicit and exhaustive. preserve-disabled is a deliberate state carrying its containment history, not neglect.

timezone.description: Explicit, so a cadence cannot be read differently by two layers.

source_definition.description: The file the definition is checked in as. The extension is whatever the host's user-level service supervisor expects; the requirement is that the definition is a checked-in file rather than state that exists only inside the supervisor.

configured_entrypoint.description: What the definition says it runs.

child_interpreter.description: The interpreter the wrapper hands work to, recorded because a wrapper and its child can drift apart.

failure_signal.description: What a failure of this job looks like from outside. An absent terminal marker is unknown, and unknown fails closed as critical.

evidence_ref.description: Where the proof of the last run lives.

interprets.description: Policy requires interpreting the job's own declared result contract. Transport success is not domain success.

points_at_disposable_worktree.description: Asserted false. Scheduled jobs aimed at worktrees that later disappear are a recurring outage class.

containment_history.description: Required when lifecycle_state is preserve-disabled or remove: why it was switched off, what would have to be true to switch it back on, and which successor took over its purpose.
